item.research_question: How to screen for single-phase high-entropy alloys using an in-house thermodynamic database and binary priority lists?
item.material_system: Co,Fe,Mn,Ni,Zn-containing high-entropy alloys (quaternary, quinary, and senary systems)
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying of elemental powders (Co >99.0%, Fe >99.99%, Mn >99.9%, Ni >99.9%, Zn >99.9%) in a planetary ball mill at 300 rpm for 30 h with 5 mm stainless balls, ball-to-powder weight ratio of 10:1, and toluene as process control agent; followed by compaction, sealing in a vacuum quartz tube, and heating at 900 °C for 24 h with a heating rate of 50 °C/min, then air cooling.
item.test_conditions: Phase identification performed using an X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation on milled powders and heat-treated samples.
key_findings: The study presents XRD raw data for milled and heat-treated Co,Fe,Mn,Ni,Zn-containing HEAs.
A comprehensive parametric study for quaternary, quinary, and senary HEAs was generated using Excel VBA codes.
Binary priority lists were developed to identify the most relevant binary sets of elements for solid solution screening.
The thermodynamic description allows exploration of the compositional space within and outside the face-centered cubic single phase solid solution stability range.
Commented files and codes are provided to replicate or modify the screening methodology in its entirety or individual steps.
item.mechanism: The authors employed an in-house thermodynamic database combined with a parametric criterion to generate binary priority lists, enabling the rapid screening of multicomponent alloys for single-phase solid solution formation.
quotes: XRD raw data of the milled and heat-treated Co,Fe,Mn,Ni,Zn-containing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) is presented.
A comprehensive parametric study for quaternary, quinary and senary HEAs is available for researchers interested in the design of HEAs.

The given thermodynamic description for Co,Fe,Mn,Ni,Zn-containing HEAs can be used for exploring this alloy system compositional space, within and outside the face-centered cubic single phase solid solution stability range.
